summary.text: Dometic RM8xxx, RMS8xxx, RML8xxx and RMSL8xxx are absorber refrigerators for caravans and motorhomes that run on mains, 12 V DC or liquid gas. Electronic MES and AES models report faults by flashing LEDs, the failure LED plus a mode or temperature LED, and AES models add an acoustic alarm.

models.text: The operating manual covers RM8xxx, RMS8xxx, RML8xxx and RMSL8xxx absorber refrigerators.

Last digit of the model number: 0 = manual energy selection with battery igniter; 1 = manual energy selection with automatic ignition (MES); 5 = automatic and manual energy selection with automatic ignition (AES).
Model code RM(S)(L) 8 5 0 1: S = stepped cabinet, L = 'Large'; width digit 4 = 486 mm, 5 = 523 mm; depth digit 0 = standard, 5 = +55 mm, 6 = +65 mm.

The rating plate inside the refrigerator shows model number, product number, serial number, electrical rating and gas pressure; quote model, product and serial number (and MLC code if applicable) to customer service.
Rated input is 135 W mains / 130 W 12 V for RM 84xx-85xx, 125 W / 120 W for RMS models and 190 W / 170 W for the 1245 mm tall RML and RMSL models.

display.text: Refrigerators with electronics (MES, AES) indicate a malfunction by the LED or display flashing; the 'Failure' LED (8) flashes at the same time, and AES models sound an acoustic alarm.
Reading the fault table: a mode LED (2 = 230 V, 3 = gas, 4 = 12 V) flashing with failure LED 8 points to supply or ignition; with temperature display 7 it points to a component fault.
Only MES and AES models have the LED fault display; RM 8xx0 battery-igniter models show the flame on a galvanometer whose pointer moves into the green range once lit.
On internal-battery power all LEDs except the GAS LED are off; the GAS LED flashes every 15 seconds, and pressing a button also lights the temperature LEDs.
A door open more than 2 minutes triggers a pulsing whistle tone; the fault table lists a 15 s acoustic signal at 2-minute intervals when the interior lighting stays on.
During the AES refuelling standby, 15 minutes after the engine is turned off, the temperature-level LEDs stay dark while all other indicators remain active.
The display dims after a few seconds without a button press; pressing a button relights it, then press again to activate the function.

reset.text: Gas or automatic mode, flame not ignited: check the gas supply (gas bottle, gas valve), then press the GAS FAILURE reset button (LED 8) after clearing the fault.
Dometic support: press the reset button for 5 seconds to reset a flame-not-ignited fault; on RMxxx6 models press it for 2 seconds until you hear a beep.
reset.locator: support page 'Fault: Flame not ignited in GAS/Automatic mode'

reset.text: MES and AES models switch on with a 2 s press of the ON/OFF button (1) and switch off with a press longer than 2 s; they restart on the last selected energy type.
AES refuelling: gas operation starts only 15 minutes after the engine is turned off; for a longer refuelling stop, switch the refrigerator off or to another energy type.

checks.text: Before notifying the service center, check that the operating instructions were followed, the refrigerator stands level, and whether it runs on any available power source.
Not cooling enough: check the ventilation grilles are not covered, set the thermostat to a higher level, check the door closes properly, and let warm food cool before storing it.
After start-up, check whether the cooling compartment works after about 4-5 hours; the freezer should be cold about one hour after switching on.
No cooling on gas: change an empty gas cylinder, open the upstream shut-off device, and for air in the gas pipe switch off and restart, 3-4 times if necessary.
After first start-up or a cylinder change, purge air by switching on the refrigerator and another gas appliance such as the stove for a short time.
No cooling on 12 V: fit a new on-board fuse, check and charge the on-board battery, and start the engine; use 12 V only while the engine runs.
No cooling on 240 V: fit a new on-board fuse and connect to mains; AES models switch to gas when mains voltage is insufficient and switch back automatically.
AES selects mains first when more than 195 V is available; priority is solar 12 V, then 240 V, then 12 V, then liquid gas.
Gas ignition faults can occur above about 1000 m (3280 ft) altitude for physical reasons; Dometic states this is no malfunction.
Compare the operating pressure on the rating plate with the pressure-reducing valve on the gas cylinder; use only liquid gas (propane, butane), not natural or town gas.

parts.text: The fault table names the 230 V and 12 V heating elements, the temperature sensor, and the burner, burner nozzles or cooling unit; replacement is arranged through Dometic Customer Service.
Automatic igniter (MES/AES): if the flame does not light, it repeats ignition twice (30 s each) at 2-minute intervals, then indicates a fault.
Manual-ignition models have an automatic flame safety valve that interrupts the gas supply about 30 seconds after the flame goes out.
Optional internal battery compartment (RM 8xx1, RM 8xx5) takes 8 x AA 1.5 V batteries and allows gas-only operation without on-board 12 V.
RM 8xx0 battery igniter uses one 1.5 V AAA/R3 battery, reached by turning the button about 90° clockwise with a screwdriver.
The gas burner must be inspected and cleaned at least once a year; on LPG the interval drops to half-yearly or quarterly.
The cooling unit uses ammonia as coolant and is under high pressure; never open the absorber cooling unit.

callTech.text: If you smell gas: open all windows and leave the room, do not operate electrical equipment, prevent naked flames, and contact authorised specialist personnel.
Coolant leak, identifiable from the strong odour: switch off the appliance, air the room thoroughly, and inform authorised customer services.
Work on gas equipment, the exhaust system and electrical facilities must be carried out by authorised personnel only; never check gas parts for leaks with an unshielded flame.
Heating element, temperature sensor, burner or cooling unit faults on the LED table: contact Customer Service and arrange replacement.
Dometic recommends maintenance after an extended shutdown of the vehicle; contact customer services.
Gas operation is not permitted at petrol stations, on ferry boats, or while the caravan or motorhome is transported by a transporter or breakdown vehicle.
